newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar dips, then ends up on fund inflows.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar dips, then ends up on fund inflows.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar reversed an early downturn to close higher against the U.S. dollar on Friday, as foreign fund inflows emerged in afternoon trade, dealers said.
The lower opening reflected the general strength of the greenback overseas, they said.
The local unit ended at its intraday high of T$27.511, off an early low of T$27.545, against Thursday's T$27.526 close. Turnover through dealers was an active US$265.5 million.
"Foreign fund entries simply beat U.S. dollar demand triggered by overseas greenback trend," said one dealer.
Dealers noted a persistent foreign fund influx in recent weeks for the bullish domestic stock market.
The stock index closed higher again on Friday, gaining 7.42 points to end at a six-year high of 8,275.57, although its rate of rise has flattened out in recent sessions.
"Investors have drawn down their foreign currency deposits in exchange for Taiwan dollars for stock investment," said one.

Dealers generally agreed the Taiwan dollar was in a stable range trade, with foreign fund inflows balancing U.S. dollar demand triggered by overseas factors. For Saturday, a range of T$27.50-27.53 was seen. -- James Peng (5080815)
